[Gunnay Screams]|quoteend=0|Haako begs Darth Vader to stop as he kills Rute Gunnay|{{Film|III}}}} '''Rute Gunnay''' was a [[Neimoidian]] [[Gender|male]] who served as an [[advisor]] to [[Trade Federation]] [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation|Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray]]. Due to their similar appearances, Gunnay was sometimes mistaken for Gunray. During the [[Clone Wars]], Gunnay also served as an [[aide]] in the [[Galactic Senate]] of the [[Galactic Republic]]. In [[19 BBY]], he was a member of the Confederacy's [[Executive Separatist Council|Separatist Council]] and was with them on the [[planet]] [[Mustafar]] when the leader of the Confederacy, [[Darth Sidious]], told the group to expect the arrival of his [[Sith apprentice|apprentice]], [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]]. Vader then [[Death|killed]] Gunnay and the rest of the council with his [[Skywalker lightsaber|lightsaber]] upon orders from Sidious. ==Biography== {{Quote|The plan has gone as you promised, my lord.''"
"''You have done well, Viceroy. When my new apprentice Darth Vader arrives, he will take care of you.|Nute Gunray and Darth Sidious|}} Rute Gunnay was a [[Neimoidian]] [[Gender|male]] who worked in the [[Trade Federation]] as an [[advisor]] to its [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation|Viceroy]], [[Nute Gunray]]. He also served as a [[Aide|senatorial aide]] in the [[Galactic Senate]] of the [[Galactic Republic]] during the [[Clone Wars]], a conflict in which the Trade Federation sided with the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]] against the Republic despite still being represented in the Senate by [[Senator]] [[Lott Dod]]. As an aide, Gunnay was responsible for writing drafts, sending sneaky messages, and managing the secret meetings of self-interested senators. By [[19 BBY]], Gunnay served as a representative of the Trade Federation on the Confederacy's [[Executive Separatist Council|Separatist Council]] along side the more senior advisor [[Rune Haako]] and Gunray. Following the [[Battle of Coruscant]], the council was moved from the [[planet]] [[Utapau]] to a [[Klegger Corp Mining Facility|mining facility]] on the planet [[Mustafar]] for their own saftey. [[Darth Sidious]], the secret master of the Confederacy, then contacted the council via [[hologram]] and spoke with Gunray as Gunnay watched. Sidious congratulated the viceroy and informed him and the rest of the council that his [[Sith apprentice|apprentice]], [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] would soon arrive to take care of them. As promised Vader, formerly the [[Jedi Knight]] Anakin Skywalker, soon arrived and was welcomed by Gunray; however, the [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Sith Lord]] then used [[the Force]] to [[Telekinesis|seal]] the doors to the room in which he, Gunnay and the other council members stood. Having been ordered to eliminate the council by Sidious, Vader then attacked with his [[Skywalker lightsaber|lightsaber]] and began cutting down everyone else in the room. As Haako cried out for mercy, Vader slashed Gunnay across the chest, causing him to scream and then collapse [[Death|dead]] by one of the room's tables. Vader then finished killing the rest of the council, including Haako and Gunray, after which the facility they had perished in was destroyed by Mustafar's [[Magma|lava]] streams. ==Personality and traits== Rute Gunnay had [[Color|green]] skin and red and golden [[eye]]s. He looked similar to Gunray, and was occasionaly mistaken for the viceroy. ==Equipment== While on Mustafar, Gunnay wore brown [[Clothing|robes]] and a brown [[Hat|miter]], garbs more somber than those of his superiors Gunray and Haako. ==Behind the scenes== ===Filming=== {{Quote|Well I rehearsed it once then when they went for a take they moved a camera crane silently in my way, with out telling me. Upon action I ran headlong into this crane knocking myself off my feet in the process… oops. Then on a retake Hayden left up the stairs forgetting to kill me off, up the stairs he realised hed forgotten some one, turned around only to see me waving at him, he poked me in the belly with his light sabre and I did a overacting dive!|Colin Ware|{{Blogspot|subdomain=echobasenews|url=2011/12/echo-base-news-interviewscolin-ware.html|name=Echo Base News|text=Echo Base News interviews Colin Ware|date=2011-12-10}}}} Rute Gunnay first appeared in the [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], which released on [[May 19]], [[2005]].''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]'' The character was portrayed by [[Colin Ware]], a make-up artist in the creature department for the film who also portrayed the Neimoidian [[Lushros Dofine]]. Prior to filming the scene in which Vader kills Gunnay, Ware and the other Separatist Council actors were given "how to die" training from the stunt supervisor, but during the first take they moved a camera crane into his way without telling him and the actor ran headfirst into the crane and was knocked to the floor. During the re-take [[Hayden Christensen]], the actor portraying Vader, forgot to strike down Ware before leaving and then turned back to find Ware waving at him. Christensen then poked Ware in the belly with his lightsaber prop and the makeup artist gave an overacted dive. ===Naming=== In the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], the character was first identified in the [[Star Wars video games|mobile card game]] ''[[Star Wars: Force Collection]]'', which initially launched in [[2013]]. Although the launch of ''Force Collection'' predates{{SW|url=news/announcing-star-wars-force-collection|text=Announcing Star Wars: Force Collection|nolive=1}} the ''Star Wars'' canon reset of [[2014]],{{SW|url=news/the-legendary-star-wars-expanded-universe-turns-a-new-page|text=The Legendary Star Wars Expanded Universe Turns a New Page}} [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] member [[Leland Chee]] confirmed that the game was kept updated to fit with canon.{{Twitter|holocronkeeper|status/846807700482666496|[[Leland Chee]]|quote=I'm not gonna go through the trouble of changing them and I don't have any reason to believe currently that anyone would. […] On the off-chance that we DID have a current need to change any of these, we would have for Force Collection.|archivedate=20210505080831}} — [[Leland Chee]] of the [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] has confirmed that [[in-universe]] information from ''[[Star Wars: Force Collection]]'' conforms with ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]]. [[File:Nute_Gunray_SWE.png|thumb|right|300px|Rute Gunnay's name is an anagram of Nute Gunray (Pictured).]] In the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, the character was erroneously identified as being Nute Gunray in the reference book ''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]'', which was written by [[James Luceno]]''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]'' and released on [[April 2]], 2005.{{SWArchive|url=episode-iii/release/publishing/news20041124.html|text=Planning Your Episode III Bookshelf}} The name was changed to "Rute Gunray" in the [[2006]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]'' before the name [[Aruteous Gunnay|Rute Gunnay]], an anagram of Nute Gunray, was then first used in the reference book ''[[Dressing a Galaxy: The Costumes of Star Wars]]'', which was written by [[Trisha Biggar]]''[[Dressing a Galaxy: The Costumes of Star Wars]]'' and released on [[October 11]], 2005.{{WebCite|url=https://www.waterstones.com/book/dressing-a-galaxy-part-1/trisha-biggar/george-lucas/9780810959644|text=Dressing a Galaxy: Part 1: The Costumes of Star Wars (Hardback)|archivedate=2022-04-24|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/mxQvt}} The character's full name was then revealed to be Aruteous Gunnay in "The Devious Neimoidians Revealed," an article in the "[[Rogues Gallery (department)|Rogues Gallery]]" department of the magazine [[Star Wars Insider 147|''Star Wars Insider'' 147]],{{InsiderCite|147|Rogues Gallery|Rogues Gallery: The Devious Neimoidians Revealed}} which was released on [[January 21]], 2014.{{TitanMagazines|url=t/star-wars-insider/us/147|text=Star Wars Insider Issue #147}} This name was suggested by the article's supervisor [[Leland Chee]] so that the character's name was not just an anagram.{{Facebook|username=star-wars-sourcebooks|url=notes/star-wars-sourcebooks/creating-naming-the-devious-neimoidians/676129629103814|name=Star
